Parent chain: systemd -> containerd-shim-runc-v2 -> psql.","process":{"pid":3017277,"uid":0,"exe":"/usr/bin/psql","args":"/usr/bin/psql -U nanosiem -d nanosiem -tAc "SELECT 1"","cwd":"/","start_ts":"2026-09-07T14:52:12.330Z","ancestry":[{"pid":2848578,"exe":"/usr/bin/containerd-shim-runc-v2"},{"pid":1,"exe":"/usr/lib/systemd/systemd"}]},"file":{"path":"/etc/<redacted>","sha256":null},"rotate":["local-password"],"explain":{"what":"psql read /etc/<redacted>.","why":"Only PAM helpers and the shadow-utils suite have any reason to read the local password hashes; anything else reading them is either already root and dumping them for offline cracking, or a misconfigured file mode you want to know about.","evidence":["hook: file_post_open on /etc/<redacted> (read)","process: /usr/bin/psql pid 3017277 uid 0 args /usr/bin/psql -U nanosiem -d nanosiem -tAc "SELECT 1"","ancestry: systemd -> containerd-shim-runc-v2 -> psql (cwd /)","actor: official, package postgresql-libs 18.6-1","context: service","rarity: common — /usr/bin/psql has read /etc: seen 3 times since 2026-09-07","the kernel refused this operation: it returned EPERM to the program, which is still running and will have seen the call fail","policy message: Local password hash database opened for reading","policy action: KPROBE_ACTION_OVERRIDE (mode enforce; a kill is only recorded once process_exit reports SIGKILL)","context: service — no controlling terminal anywhere in the chain; root is systemd","not in allowlist: none of the 82 rule(s) in /etc/moat/allowlist.d matches exe=/usr/bin/psql file=/etc/<redacted>"],"expected":"The user database service reads it constantly: systemd-userdbd and the systemd-userwork workers it forks opened /etc/<redacted> seven times in fifteen seconds on a normal login, and sddm-helper reads it on every unlock. Change every local password (`passwd`), and treat any that was reused elsewhere as public.","If this was you, run one of the ignore commands above; otherwise `moatctl ack <id>` once you have finished checking."]},"action_taken":"blocked","actions":["kill","ignore"],"acked":false,"mode":"enforce","actor":{"provenance":"official","package":"postgresql-libs 18.6-1"},"context":"service","severity_base":"critical","severity_reason":"critical: no adjustment applied (actor official, context service)","surface":"alerts","tier":"detection","pkg_install_escalation":false,"suppressed_by":null,"rarity":"common","rarity_text":"/usr/bin/psql has read /etc: seen 3 times since 2026-09-07","triage":{"agent":"claude","at":"2026-09-07T17:31:50.951Z","verdict":"benign","confidence":"high","summary":"This is the nanosiem dev stack's PostgreSQL container: libpq client tools (psql, and later pg_isready) run on a 5-second loop as root inside the `postgres:18` container and do a getpwuid_r user lookup at startup, which glibc's NSS path touches the shadow database for. The read was refused with EPERM, no hashes were disclosed, and the whole 998-alert cluster comes from that one container and nothing else.","reasoning":"Mechanism end to end. The accused argv is exactly `psql -U nanosiem -d nanosiem -tAc "SELECT 1"`, parented directly by containerd-shim-runc-v2 pid 2848578 (no `sh`, i.e. a `docker exec`), cwd /, uid 0, no controlling terminal. That command is verbatim the wait-for-Postgres loop in this repo: ~/Projects/nanosiem/scripts/start-microservices-dev.sh:466-474 runs `docker exec -e PGPASSWORD=... $NANO_DEV_POSTGRES_CONTAINER psql -U ... -d ... -tAc 'SELECT 1'` in an `until ...; do sleep 1; done`, and the same file's non-reuse branch plus docker-compose.yml:32-36 (`test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U nanosiem -d nanosiem"]`, `interval: 5s`) accounts for the pg_isready half of the cluster — which is why every alert lands on a 5.0s cadence. I read the staged tree.txt/net.txt for a sibling alert from the identical shim pid 2848578 (incident 01M1YCNMAV4MYNXNTJE4BJRG1J): systemd -> containerd-shim-runc-v2 (namespace moby, container 6095717ca3f0...) -> /bin/sh -c "pg_isready -U nanosiem" -> pg_isready, and 'no matching rows' in the socket table — the tree owns no network sockets at all. Why /etc/<redacted>: I grepped the staged actor.psql.suspect (as data, not executed). It self-identifies as PostgreSQL 18.6 (matching host package postgresql-libs 18.6-1 and the postgres:18 image) and imports getpwuid/getpwuid_r; it contains no literal '/etc/<redacted>' or '/etc/passwd' string and no exfil tooling (curl/wget/nc/base64) — so nothing in the binary deliberately targets the password file. The touch is the NSS user-database lookup libpq does at connection setup (home dir for ~/.pgpass, default auth name) running as uid 0, against /etc/nsswitch.conf's `shadow: files systemd`; the process is in the container's mount namespace, so the file opened is the image's /etc/<redacted>, not the host's. Provenance and history corroborate: /var/log/pacman.log:1095 shows postgresql-libs 18.6-1 installed 2026-09-01 from the signed official repo with no package transaction today, so nothing was freshly dropped. In alerts.jsonl, every single alert whose parent chain contains containerd-shim-runc-v2 is this same shadow-read from psql or pg_isready — 998 of them, zero net/exec/persist/pkg events from that container tree — and moat's own noise guard has since demoted the rule to the timeline (rarity: pg_isready 1208 reads of /etc since 2026-09-07). A credential dumper does not re-issue the identical failing open every 5 seconds for hours after being EPERM'd, with no socket, no second-stage exec, and no other behaviour. The interleaved moat-exec-untrusted-home entries in the +/-5min window belong to the developer's cargo/codex build tree (a different ancestry, already triaged under 01M1Y3ZF7NEM36B0BBR26BBPE1) and are not part of this process tree. Two gaps I could not close, neither of which changes the verdict: this incident's own process.json/tree.txt/net.txt are listed in the alert record but are not present on disk (I substituted the sibling from the same shim), and the target's contents are withheld by design. Caveat on the fix: allowlisting is path-keyed, so an exe rule for /usr/bin/psql would also cover any future binary at that path — exe+file keeps it as narrow as this bundle supports.","proposed_allowlist":"[[rule]]

file = "/etc/<redacted>"
